issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers defines a method named appendElement(T[] array, T element) but other template classes (e.g., Stock.java) call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This name/signature mismatch means the template code will not compile and prevents students from using the ArrayHelpers utility as the problem statement recommends.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ArrayHelpers API consistent across the template. Either rename the method in ArrayHelpers from appendElement to addElementToArray (matching calls in Stock.java and solution), or update all callers to use appendElement. Prefer updating ArrayHelpers to provide a method named addElementToArray with the same signature to match existing usages.

issues.description: The helper method for appending an element to an array is named differently between artifacts: the template's ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(...) while both the template's Stock class and the solution's ArrayHelpers use the name addElementToArray(...). This mismatch creates confusion and compilation errors in the template and makes it unclear which method name students should use when following the problem and comparing to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Rename the template's ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (or change the Stock usage to call appendElement) so that ArrayHelpers provides addElementToArray(...) as used by Stock.java and the solution. This will remove the naming mismatch and avoid compilation/confusion for students.
